question_text:
Saddie is trying to determine the cost of repairing his car's engine. The cost of repairs can be represented by the rational function C(x) = (2x+7) / ((x+3)(x+1)), where C(x) is the cost of repairs in dollars and x represents the number of hours of labor. Saddie knows that the cost of repairs consists of the cost of work on determining the cause of the breakdown, D(x) = A / (x+3), and the cost of work on eliminating the cause of the breakdown, E(x) = B / (x+1).
Which equation can be used to find A and B?
current_state: The question is about partial fraction decomposition. The rational function C(x) is given as C(x) = D(x) + E(x). This translates to (2x+7) / ((x+3)(x+1)) = A / (x+3) + B / (x+1). To find A and B, one must combine the fractions on the right side by finding a common denominator, which is (x+3)(x+1). This results in A(x+1) + B(x+3) / ((x+3)(x+1)). Equating the numerators of both sides yields 2x+7 = A(x+1) + B(x+3). This matches option B. Option B is also highlighted as the chosen answer. The explanation provided beneath the hint section correctly shows this derivation.
